r: The course builds beginning Mandarin — pronunciation, distinguishing the four tones, speaking, listening, and character writing — toward functional communicative competence. The applied task most exposed here is cross-language rendering: task-exposure research classifies translators and interpreters among the most-exposed occupations, and machine translation for Mandarin is already strong, which pushes the instrumental case for language study downward when the task is treated as translation. But the course's aim is the student's own human communicative competence, part of it embodied oral practice mapping to O*NET activities like establishing interpersonal relationships and communicating with persons outside the organization — categories observed-usage data shows least represented. It also carries a General Studies Oral Communication designation and scaffolds the CHI sequence. At 24 months the need to build communicative competence is not eroded by translation tools; rating Low.

By 2031, real-time speech translation will plausibly be excellent and ubiquitous, materially eroding the instrumental rationale for learning Mandarin to perform translation or basic cross-language transactions — a legitimate downward pressure this rating registers, since task-exposure evidence places translation near the top of exposed work. What survives is a student's own embodied communicative competence for real-time interpersonal and culturally situated exchange, plus the course's foundational role in the language sequence and its oral-communication general-education function. The GT-Pathways designation and scaffolding cap the erosion, and verification of nuance in tone-dependent Mandarin still favors human command. The rating rises to Medium: translation-as-task is largely automatable on this horizon, but embodied oral competence and the general-education lock keep the course instrumentally relevant. Confidence is lower here, as reasonable analysts could read the erosion as stronger.

A decade out, the central case has seamless AI translation pervasive across text and speech, so the instrumental case for elementary Mandarin as a translation tool is substantially eroded — among the clearer catalog examples of AI performing the applied task. What remains is the value of direct human command of the language for interpersonal, cultural, and unscripted real-time contexts where speaking oneself matters, alongside the general-education requirement in the central case. The rating holds Medium rather than High, capped by the oral-communication designation and the residue of embodied practice rather than by capability. The uncertainty is genuine: capability trends suggest fast progress, and this is a case where stronger erosion is plausible, so the confidence flag is low. No confident point-prediction is warranted; the direction is downward, the binding brake the general-education mandate.
CHI 1010.d: This is an introductory course in Chinese that stresses pronunciation, speaking, listening, and writing. Attention is given to the sound system of Chinese to enable students to distinguish the four tones and to develop and use functional, communicative language skills. Open to students with no previous experience in Chinese

r: This continuation develops listening, speaking, reading, and writing with emphasis on functional, communicative language for oral and written proficiency and cultural competency. As with the first course, the exposed applied task is cross-language rendering: task-exposure research ranks translators among the most-exposed workers, and Mandarin machine translation already performs routine conversion competently, pressing the translation rationale down. But the course targets the student's own communicative and cultural competence, including embodied oral practice that maps to O*NET activities like establishing interpersonal relationships and communicating with persons outside the organization — work observed-usage data shows least automated. It carries General Studies Arts and Humanities and Global Diversity designations and builds prerequisite proficiency for the sequence. At 24 months the instrumental need to acquire communicative competence is not displaced by translation tools, and the general-education designation adds near-term inertia; rating Low.

By 2031, fluent real-time translation will substantially erode the instrumental reason to study Mandarin for cross-language transactional tasks — reading signage, drafting simple correspondence, basic interpretation — which this course partly serves, and task-exposure evidence supports registering that pressure. What persists is the learner's own capacity for spontaneous, culturally competent interpersonal exchange and the course's foundational role advancing students toward intermediate work. The Arts and Humanities general-education designation and the sequence-scaffolding function cap erosion at Medium. Verification also matters: in tone- and character-dependent Mandarin, non-obvious failures in machine output still reward human command, consistent with the jagged-frontier finding that over-trusting AI outside its reliable range degrades accuracy. The rating rises to Medium, reflecting largely automatable translation against durable embodied and general-education value. Confidence is lower for language courses, where erosion could reasonably be judged steeper.

A decade out, pervasive AI translation makes the transactional cross-language uses of elementary Mandarin substantially automatable, eroding that portion of the course's instrumental case. What survives is direct human proficiency for unscripted interpersonal, cultural, and professional exchange where speaking and understanding oneself carries the interaction, plus the general-education requirement in the central case. The rating holds Medium rather than High, capped by the Arts and Humanities and Global Diversity designations and the embodied-communication residue, not by any ceiling on capability, which capability-trend evidence suggests will keep advancing. The uncertainty is real and the confidence flag low: this is a course where analysts could reasonably see stronger erosion toward High as translation becomes frictionless. No confident 10-year point-prediction is offered; the direction is a measured downward drift held at Medium by the transfer mandate.
CHI 1020.d: This course is a continuation of CHI 1010 and focuses on skills development in listening, speaking, reading, and writing with emphasis on the use of functional, communicative language for oral and written proficiency and cultural competency.

r: This one-credit professional supplement to Elementary Chinese II pursues two applied aims: communicating in specific, career-relevant situations in Mandarin, and developing intercultural expertise for effective communication with people from diverse cultural backgrounds. The language-transaction half is exposed — task-exposure research places translation among the most-exposed activities, and machine translation handles routine workplace phrasing competently. But the course's center of gravity is embodied, real-time intercultural communication, mapping to O*NET activities like establishing and maintaining interpersonal relationships and communicating with persons outside the organization — precisely the low-exposure, presence-dependent work observed-usage data shows least automated. It carries an Arts and Humanities general-education designation. At 24 months the instrumental need to build human intercultural competence is not met by translation tools, and the interpersonal core keeps realized exposure low; rating Low.

By 2031, real-time translation will absorb much of the career-relevant language-transaction content — drafting messages, interpreting routine exchanges — a pressure the rating registers. Yet the course's distinctive object, intercultural expertise for effective face-to-face communication across cultural difference, is real-time interpersonal work that AI advises but does not perform for the student: reading a counterpart's cues, adjusting register, and building rapport remain embodied tasks. That presence-dependence, the low-exposure profile task-exposure research assigns such interpersonal activity, and the general-education designation together hold the rating at Low even as the translation component erodes. The jagged-frontier evidence reinforces this: over-relying on AI for culturally sensitive judgment outside its reliable range degrades outcomes, keeping human competence necessary. The rating stays Low; confidence is lower given how quickly the translation-transaction share could grow.

A decade out, AI translation and cross-cultural drafting will be pervasive, substantially eroding the language-transaction rationale of this professional supplement. What resists automation is the embodied intercultural competence at the course's core — spontaneous, presence-dependent communication and rapport-building across cultural difference — which the central case still leaves to the human participant. That residue and the Arts and Humanities designation cap the rating at Medium rather than High. The uncertainty is genuine: capability-trend evidence suggests fast progress, and if AI mediation of intercultural exchange becomes seamless the instrumental case could erode further than Medium; equally, the interpersonal core could prove durable. No confident 10-year point-prediction is warranted. The measured read is a downward drift to Medium, held above High by the embodied, real-time interpersonal center that distinguishes this course from the pure elementary-language offerings. Confidence is low.
CHI 1021.d: This one-credit course complements the existing CHI 1020 - Elementary Chinese II or its equivalent. It adds a professional dimension to the study of Chinese, with two main objectives: enhancing students' ability to communicate in specific, career- relevant situations in the target language, and developing intercultural expertise for effective communication with individuals from diverse cultural backgrounds.
